STRICT READ-ONLY task. Do not write, edit, or create any file anywhere except your own scratch (none needed — just return text). Do not touch git state (read-only git commands like `git log`, `git show`, `git diff` are fine; no checkout/reset/commit).

CONTEXT: live-spec (repo at /Users/sashaabramovich/live-spec) is a spec-driven product-development pack being productized. Its owner (communicates mostly in Russian) has repeatedly described, in his own words during working sessions, an "intake chain": a request comes in → it becomes a feature (found existing or opened new) → the feature is linked into ARCHITECTURE.md → linked into TEST_MATRIX.md → classified (сквозной [cross-cutting] vs локальный [local]; новый [new] vs правка [amendment]; раздел [section] vs подфункционал [sub-function]) → from that classification follows what to update, which tests to add, and whether to run the whole suite or only the matrix rows for that feature.

YOUR JOB: find and quote VERBATIM (in the original Russian where applicable, with an English gloss alongside if helpful) every place the owner personally prescribes or describes this chain — in his own chat messages, not the assistant's summaries of it. Cite each quote with its source (file path + timestamp/line, or file path + line number for docs).

SOURCES TO SEARCH (in priority order — budget your reading, do not read entire huge files linearly, grep/extract selectively):

1. The 20 LARGEST working-session transcripts (jsonl, Claude Code format) — these are real working sessions, not judge/audit noise. Use the extractor at /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-tmp-live-spec-roadmap-wave/4e60d161-3c51-44f3-9cf0-44b9e9f4e501/scratchpad/extract.py, e.g.:
   python3 extract.py FILE.jsonl --max-chars 700 > /tmp/out.txt
   then grep the output for keywords (case-insensitive, try multiple): фича, feature, ARCHITECTURE, TEST_MATRIX, линк, link, классиф, сквозн, локальн, матриц, traceability, "какие тесты", "гонять", "весь suite", "все тесты", "строки матрицы", intake, запрос

OUTPUT: a compact plain-text report (in Russian, since this feeds a Russian-language deliverable) with:
- Section "Прескрипции хозяина" — bulleted VERBATIM quotes, each with source citation
- Note any variation/evolution across time (did the chain's description change between sessions?)
- Keep total length reasonable — prioritize quality/verbatim-accuracy over volume, aim for the 10-20 strongest quotes rather than exhaustive collection

Budget yourself to roughly 80k-100k tokens of tool use. Report back your findings as your final message (do not write any files).

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# The pipeline walk
2	
3	This page walks one change through the full pipeline, station by station. The order is fixed: spec →
4	prove → architecture → prove architecture → matrix → test → code → verify → commit & show. The
5	normative home for every step is the build-pipeline skill (`skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md`); the
6	shared rules every station obeys live once in `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md`. This page explains the
7	walk in plain words and points there for the letter of each law.
8	
9	## Station 1 — a wish arrives
10	
11	- **Enters:** a request from the human, spoken in chat or dropped as one file in the project's
12	  `inbox/` folder (the parallel-safe door for anything born outside the assigned session).
13	- **Produces:** one intake line before any tool call: size, priority, the door (feature · bug ·
14	  refactor · docs-only · skip), the work-kind (product · infra · skill · prose), and the wish's place
15	  on the feature map. The line is echoed back to the human and the wish becomes a queue row. A wish
16	  carrying several user stories splits here, one row per story (SPEC T-17).
17	- **Owner:** build-pipeline (step zero); feedback-intake sweeps the inbox itself.
18	- **Blocks:** work stays parked until the door is named. Hard tripwires decide the door by rule — a
19	  new visible surface, new persistent state, a new interaction, or behaviour with no spec clause
20	  behind it means the feature door, however casually the wish was phrased (SPEC T-12, INV-16).
21	
22	## Station 2 — spec delta
23	
24	- **Enters:** the classified wish and the current `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`.
25	- **Produces:** a spec delta in plain product language: the scenario the person walks, entities,
26	  states, transitions, invariants, and how the touched surface composes with its neighbours. A
27	  feature delta opens with regression fences (neighbouring promises that must stay true) and closes
28	  with two sentences: non-goals and one success measure. Real gaps become a marked open question
29	  (`⟨DECIDE⟩`) with a recommended pick.
30	- **Owner:** spec-author writes the spec; it is the authoring half of a pair.
31	- **Blocks:** code before spec is banned; a spec written after the code documents whatever got built,
32	  and the reviewer at the next station can no longer catch the difference.
33	
34	## Station 3 — prover review of the spec
35	
36	- **Enters:** the fresh spec delta.
37	- **Produces:** a structured review with formal-verification thinking (states, transitions,
38	  invariants, composition), written to `docs/prover/YYYY-MM-DD.md` with a folded / rejected column
39	  per finding, so the folding is verifiable after a memory wipe.
40	- **Owner:** product-prover, the reviewing half of the pair. It reads documents; the test suite
41	  proves what the artifact does.
42	- **Blocks:** every defect finding is folded into the spec before the walk continues. Open
43	  questions the change touches are resolved or asked; the rest are listed, and they carry no gate.
44	
45	## Station 4 — architecture delta
46	
47	- **Enters:** the proven spec.
48	- **Produces:** an updated `ARCHITECTURE.md`: named nodes with one responsibility each, every spec
49	  fact owned by exactly one node, named seams between nodes, quality budgets with the place their
50	  real numbers can be read, a runtime view that walks every promised flow, and a placement view that
51	  says where each node runs. In a live codebase every node pins to a `file:line` that came from a
52	  command actually run.
53	- **Owner:** build-pipeline (step 3). A small change cites its existing node and moves on.
54	- **Blocks:** a spec fact with no owning node, or a node with no spec backing, is a defect found at
55	  the next station.
56	
57	## Station 5 — prover pass on the architecture
58	
59	- **Enters:** the changed architecture doc.
60	- **Produces:** findings in the same `docs/prover/` record, from six checks: every fact owned · no
61	  unbacked node · every seam names what crosses it · budgets stated with their measurement homes ·
62	  the runtime view walks every flow · the placement view covers every node.
63	- **Owner:** product-prover, with the architecture lens.
64	- **Blocks:** the same folding discipline as station 3. The pass runs whenever the doc changed;
65	  a change that touched no structure stands this station down by name in the landing report.
66	
67	## Station 6 — test matrix rows
68	
69	- **Enters:** the proven spec and the proven architecture.
70	- **Produces:** rows in `TEST_MATRIX.md`, derived, never hand-filled: one block per architecture
71	  node, every spec fact with at least one row, every row stating both what the fact does and what it
72	  must never do (the never side is the regression fence), and every row pinned to a test level —
73	  string, DOM-text, browser-computed, or pixel. The matrix opens with an inventory of every file the
74	  user receives, and derivation closes by walking the coverage checklist.
75	- **Owner:** test-author (pipeline step 5).
76	- **Blocks:** a fact with no row, or a row at too weak a level, is a derivation defect fixed here.
77	  Any fact about visibility, layout, colour, or interaction needs level browser-computed or above.
78	
79	## Station 7 — red-first tests
80	
81	- **Enters:** the derived matrix rows.
82	- **Produces:** one owning test per row, asserting the real shipped artifact — the rendered page, the
83	  produced file, the actual function output. Each new test is watched failing first; the red run is
84	  the proof it can catch the missing behaviour.
85	- **Owner:** test-author (pipeline step 6).
86	- **Blocks:** a test that never went red proves nothing yet. Editing a test to make a change pass is
87	  banned.
88	
89	## Station 8 — code
90	
91	- **Enters:** the red tests and the spec sentences they serve.
92	- **Produces:** the implementation, driven until the suite is green. Mechanical, well-scoped work
93	  goes to a cheaper junior worker with a self-contained brief and a persistent checkpoint file;
94	  judgment stays with the senior, who verifies the worker's result by deed.
95	- **Owner:** build-pipeline (step 7), as a senior developer.
96	- **Blocks:** green tests are the exit condition; the next station adds eyes.
97	
98	## Station 9 — verify by deed
99	
100	- **Enters:** the green implementation.
101	- **Produces:** a verify-by-deed record: the builder runs the real thing and looks at the result with
102	  fresh eyes. Every check the diff can reach runs before any push (SPEC INV-45). For gated prose,
103	  `scripts/spec-done-gate.py` runs the prose gate; its conditions are described in
104	  [docs/push-law.md](push-law.md).
105	- **Owner:** build-pipeline (step 8), backed by the mechanical guardrails on the pre-push hook.
106	- **Blocks:** green means zero failures and the skip list exactly matches the pinned expected set; an
107	  unexpected skip is a failure outright. Red at a pause is never committed — the failing test name
108	  plus a hypothesis becomes the top `NEXT_STEPS.md` item.
109	
110	## Station 10 — commit
111	
112	- **Enters:** a green tree with no regression.
113	- **Produces:** the commit, a patch-level version bump by default, and the docs travelling in the
114	  same change: the readme, the changelog in the user's terms, the journal entry with the dated why.
115	- **Owner:** build-pipeline (step 9), as a careful release hand.
116	- **Blocks:** the concurrent-edit fence runs before the commit — `git status` and HEAD re-checked
117	  against what was last read. Gates the human personally named wait for the human's word.
118	
119	## Station 11 — show the result
120	
121	- **Enters:** the committed change.
122	- **Produces:** the real render opened for the human in a new window, with real data, plus a landing
123	  report: what landed, where it sits on the map, which taste defaults were picked (told plainly, with
124	  no confirmation requested), and every stood-down step named.
125	- **Owner:** communicator shapes the human-facing exchange; feedback-intake catches what comes back.
126	- **Blocks:** a push or deposit waits until the human has had the work in front of them, and a bare
127	  file path never counts as showing.
128	
129	## When the pipeline may be shortcut
130	
131	A tiny edit skips the pipeline only when all three hold: it touches a single file, it adds no new
132	state, element, or user-visible behaviour, and an existing test level already covers the touched fact.
133	Even then the edit still ships a test. A bug takes a shorter road — bug → matrix → test → code — with
134	a red-on-bug test first and a cite of the existing architecture node it lands in. Anything touching
135	visibility, layout, or colour enters at the matrix station at minimum.
136	
137	The rules decide, ahead of anyone's mood: the tripwires at station 1 outrank a casual "it's just a
138	one-liner", and urgency moves a wish's priority while its door stays put. When the shortcut boundary
139	is genuinely unclear, the session asks the human one plain question and does not guess
140	(build-pipeline's skip boundary; SPEC T-12).
141

  behind it means the feature door, however casually the wish was phrased (SPEC T-12, INV-16).

## Station 2 — spec delta

- **Enters:** the classified wish and the current `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`.
- **Produces:** a spec delta in plain product language: the scenario the person walks, entities,
  states, transitions, invariants, and how the touched surface composes with its neighbours. A
  feature delta opens with regression fences (neighbouring promises that must stay true) and closes
  with two sentences: non-goals and one success measure. Real gaps become a marked open question
  (`⟨DECIDE⟩`) with a recommended pick.
- **Owner:** spec-author writes the spec; it is the authoring half of a pair.
- **Blocks:** code before spec is banned; a spec written after the code documents whatever got built,
  and the reviewer at the next station can no longer catch the difference.

## Station 3 — prover review of the spec

- **Enters:** the fresh spec delta.
- **Produces:** a structured review with formal-verification thinking (states, transitions,
  invariants, composition), written to `docs/prover/YYYY-MM-DD.md` with a folded / rejected column
  per finding, so the folding is verifiable after a memory wipe.
- **Owner:** product-prover, the reviewing half of the pair. It reads documents; the test suite
  proves what the artifact does.
- **Blocks:** every defect finding is folded into the spec before the walk continues. Open
  questions the change touches are resolved or asked; the rest are listed, and they carry no gate.

## Station 4 — architecture delta

- **Enters:** the proven spec.
- **Produces:** an updated `ARCHITECTURE.md`: named nodes with one responsibility each, every spec
  fact owned by exactly one node, named seams between nodes, quality budgets with the place their
  real numbers can be read, a runtime view that walks every promised flow, and a placement view that
  says where each node runs. In a live codebase every node pins to a `file:line` that came from a
  command actually run.
- **Owner:** build-pipeline (step 3). A small change cites its existing node and moves on.
- **Blocks:** a spec fact with no owning node, or a node with no spec backing, is a defect found at
  the next station.

## Station 5 — prover pass on the architecture

- **Enters:** the changed architecture doc.
- **Produces:** findings in the same `docs/prover/` record, from six checks: every fact owned · no
  unbacked node · every seam names what crosses it · budgets stated with their measurement homes ·
  the runtime view walks every flow · the placement view covers every node.
- **Owner:** product-prover, with the architecture lens.
- **Blocks:** the same folding discipline as station 3. The pass runs whenever the doc changed;
  a change that touched no structure stands this station down by name in the landing report.

## Station 6 — test matrix rows

- **Enters:** the proven spec and the proven architecture.
- **Produces:** rows in `TEST_MATRIX.md`, derived, never hand-filled: one block per architecture
  node, every spec fact with at least one row, every row stating both what the fact does and what it
  must never do (the never side is the regression fence), and every row pinned to a test level —
  string, DOM-text, browser-computed, or pixel. The matrix opens with an inventory of every file the
  user receives, and derivation closes by walking the coverage checklist.
- **Owner:** test-author (pipeline step 5).
- **Blocks:** a fact with no row, or a row at too weak a level, is a derivation defect fixed here.
  Any fact about visibility, layout, colour, or interaction needs level browser-computed or above.

## Station 7 — red-first tests

- **Enters:** the derived matrix rows.
- **Produces:** one owning test per row, asserting the real shipped artifact — the rendered page, the
  produced file, the actual function output. Each new test is watched failing first; the red run is
  the proof it can catch the missing behaviour.
- **Owner:** test-author (pipeline step 6).
- **Blocks:** a test that never went red proves nothing yet. Editing a test to make a change pass is
  banned.

## Station 8 — code

- **Enters:** the red tests and the spec sentences they serve.
- **Produces:** the implementation, driven until the suite is green. Mechanical, well-scoped work
  goes to a cheaper junior worker with a self-contained brief and a persistent checkpoint file;
  judgment stays with the senior, who verifies the worker's result by deed.
- **Owner:** build-pipeline (step 7), as a senior developer.
- **Blocks:** green tests are the exit condition; the next station adds eyes.

## Station 9 — verify by deed

- **Enters:** the green implementation.
- **Produces:** a verify-by-deed record: the builder runs the real thing and looks at the result with
  fresh eyes. Every check the diff can reach runs before any push (SPEC INV-45). For gated prose,
  `scripts/spec-done-gate.py` runs the prose gate; its conditions are described in
  [docs/push-law.md](push-law.md).
- **Owner:** build-pipeline (step 8), backed by the mechanical guardrails on the pre-push hook.
- **Blocks:** green means zero failures and the skip list exactly matches the pinned expected set; an
  unexpected skip is a failure outright. Red at a pause is never committed — the failing test name
  plus a hypothesis becomes the top `NEXT_STEPS.md` item.

## Station 10 — commit

- **Enters:** a green tree with no regression.
- **Produces:** the commit, a patch-level version bump by default, and the docs travelling in the
  same change: the readme, the changelog in the user's terms, the journal entry with the dated why.
- **Owner:** build-pipeline (step 9), as a careful release hand.
- **Blocks:** the concurrent-edit fence runs before the commit — `git status` and HEAD re-checked
  against what was last read. Gates the human personally named wait for the human's word.

## Station 11 — show the result

- **Enters:** the committed change.
- **Produces:** the real render opened for the human in a new window, with real data, plus a landing
  report: what landed, where it sits on the map, which taste defaults were picked (told plainly, with
  no confirmation requested), and every stood-down step named.
- **Owner:** communicator shapes the human-facing exchange; feedback-intake catches what comes back.
- **Blocks:** a push or deposit waits until the human has had the work in front of them, and a bare
  file path never counts as showing.

## When the pipeline may be shortcut

A tiny edit skips the pipeline only when all three hold: it touches a single file, it adds no new
state, element, or user-visible behaviour, and an existing test level already covers the touched fact.
Even then the edit still ships a test. A bug takes a shorter road — bug → matrix → test → code — with
a red-on-bug test first and a cite of the existing architecture node it lands in. Anything touching
visibility, layout, or colour enters at the matrix station at minimum.

The rules decide, ahead of anyone's mood: the tripwires at station 1 outrank a casual "it's just a
one-liner", and urgency moves a wish's priority while its door stays put. When the shortcut boundary
is genuinely unclear, the session asks the human one plain question and does not guess
(build-pipeline's skip boundary; SPEC T-12).

Mode: **CROSS-LINK** on the three new clauses landed together (queue rows 77 + 85, one landing):

- **T-15** (SPEC L61–66) — you may name an **appetite** at intake ("half a day", "a week"); it rides the
  intake line next to size and priority; scope bends to fit the appetite, never the reverse — the moment
  the walk sees the wish won't fit, it "comes back with the trimmed version for you to choose", never a
  silent overrun, never a silently thinner result; no appetite named ⇒ none assumed; the facet sweep's
  defaults [T-13] size themselves to a named appetite (plainest default for a half-day, considered option
  for two weeks).
- **INV-20** (SPEC L152–155) — every feature's spec-delta closes with a one-sentence **non-goals** ("version
  comparison — not this time") so a reader/prover can tell a refusal from a hole; "absent non-goals mean
  nothing was excluded on purpose, and the prover reads silence as a hole again."
- **INV-21** (SPEC L156–161) — every feature also states one **success measure** ("opens the evidence panel
  once per session"), decided or `[default]`-tagged like any facet; the quantification questions ride the
  facet sweep's batched report [T-13, INV-18]; the machinery that READS the measures (KPI/A-B/segmentation)
  is [target] under its own rows — until it lands, a success measure is a written promise checked by eye.
- Three Formal-index rows (T-15 L563, INV-20 L583, INV-21 L584) + header bump v0.12.0 → v0.13.0 (L1).

Seams checked (task item 4): **T-15 vs INV-12/T-12** (does appetite become a third axis of the ONE intake
line? does it collide with "quick win"?); **T-15 vs T-11** (does a small appetite jump the queue?); **T-15
"comes back … for you to choose" vs INV-4** (does the trim question park the lane?); **T-15 vs INV-18**
(appetite trims scope — can it drop a facet?); **INV-20 vs INV-18 / prover hole-hunting** ("silence is a
hole" vs "silence is not an option"); **INV-20 surfacing vs INV-5 / T-7 / T-8**; **INV-21 `[default]` vs
INV-18** (same tag, matrix-row implication); **INV-21 [target] machinery vs S-0** (granularity); **adoption**
(A-3/A-10 — retroactive measures?); **prototype** (E-17/INV-17 — no measures for sketches?).

**Prior-record check (task item 5).** `2026-07-05-fences.md`: all 8 findings **FOLDED same sitting**;
closing line "Nothing left for the queue from this pass." **Zero unfolded rows carried forward.** The
MINOR-under-CROSS-LINK FULL debt it (and `-facets`) recorded is owed at the 1.0 milestone FULL audit — not
a per-finding fold. Nothing owed into this pass.

**Mechanical guard.** Delta anchor↔prose symmetry exact: T-15 (prose L66 / index L563), INV-20 (prose L155
/ index L583), INV-21 (prose L161 / index L584) — each appears once per direction; no duplicate anchors;
index one-liners track the prose. Header bumped v0.12.0 → v0.13.0. The new clauses reverse no earlier-proven
material — the seams below are one model-collision (F1), gaps, and wording reconciliations, not
contradictions of proven law.

**Done well (noted, no finding).** INV-21 scopes its `[target]` to the reading MACHINERY alone, leaving the
success-measure WRITING live (every feature states one NOW, checked by eye) — this respects S-0's
granularity rule exactly (the tag binds at its own clause, not the parent concept), and the index row
mirrors it ("reading machinery [target]"). INV-21 also correctly routes its quantification questions to the
existing INV-18 batched report rather than inventing a second channel.

**Process note (MINOR bump under CROSS-LINK).** The bump 0.12.0 → 0.13.0 is a MINOR (`0.x.0`) step, and the
prover skill requires a FULL re-prove before any MINOR bump (M-1). As with the `-facets` and `-fences`
precedents: the CROSS-LINK delta stands; the FULL whole-spec pass owed by the MINOR gate discharges at the
**M-6 push gate for this landing** (or the 1.0 milestone FULL audit), not here. Recorded so it is not lost.

**Worker verdict: 1 must-fix · 6 should-clarify · 2 worth-considering.** Per M-6 the must-fix (F1) folds
before the push, or the delta does not ship. Outcomes **PENDING** — the senior triages.

| # | Finding (one line) | Severity | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | **The appetite trim "comes back for you to choose" reads as a lane-blocking gate — a head-on tension with INV-4.** T-15: "the moment the walk sees the wish won't fit its budget, it **comes back with the trimmed version for you to choose** — … never a **silently thinner result**" (L64). INV-4 (L173): "**A pending question for you never stops the work** — the lane proceeds on the recommended option; the question stays open in the row." As worded, T-15's "for you to choose" is a human gate that WAITS (else it ships a trim you didn't choose = "silently thinner"), which parks the lane — the exact thing INV-4 forbids. But if the lane proceeds on the recommended trim per INV-4, it delivers the thinner result before you answer — which T-15 calls "silently thinner." The two cannot both hold as literally worded; an implementer cannot tell whether an over-budget wish blocks or proceeds. Fix by the INV-18 precedent (defaults, L128–131), which is the exact analog: the lane **proceeds on the walk's RECOMMENDED trim** (INV-4), **surfaced in the batched report** so it is not silent (INV-5 — "silently" here means unsurfaced, not un-chosen), and your **re-widen becomes a new wish** — the trim never parks the lane. Reword T-15 to route the trim through INV-4/INV-5 exactly as INV-18 routes a defaulted facet. | must-fix · internal-conflict (consistency) | **FOLDED**: the trim proceeds on the recommended option, surfaced in the batched report (INV-18 precedent); re-widen = a new wish; the lane never parks (T-15 reworded) |
| F2 | **The "ONE intake line" is now enumerated three ways, and T-15 changed none of the two priors.** T-1..T-7 (L48): "classified by **size, priority, and door** — stated back to you in one INTAKE line." T-12 (L77): "A row carries **two axes**, stated together in ONE intake line — **size · priority · door**." T-15 (L63): appetite "rides the intake line **next to size and priority**." The intake line is a named surface (one-surface-one-name), but its CONTENTS are stated as "size·priority·door" in two homes and T-15 silently adds a fourth item — T-12 even asserts a closed "two axes," which appetite now over-runs. A reader/implementer cannot tell whether appetite is a third axis, an optional rider on the size axis, or a fourth co-equal field. Fix: pin appetite's status in ONE home (recommend: an OPTIONAL rider on the size/effort axis — it caps effort, it is not a new "where it enters" axis like the door), and update T-12's enumeration to "size · priority · door (· appetite when named)" so the three statements agree. | should-clarify · boundary-issue (composition) | **FOLDED**: appetite = optional RIDER on the size word; T-12 enumeration updated ("size (with its optional appetite rider) · priority · door") |
| F3 | **Appetite is never said to be order-neutral — "give it half a day" reads as "do it soon" and collides with quick-win.** T-15 places appetite "next to size and priority" (L63) but says nothing about lane ORDER; T-11 (L68–75) is the sole home of ordering (critical heads, quick win bubbles once, then queue head). Appetite is an effort/scope CAP, not urgency — yet a reader (or the classifier) can read a small appetite as a fast-track, and a "half-day" appetite looks indistinguishable from the **quick win** priority ("low effort, immediate value" — L56), so the two silently conflate. Nothing states a small appetite grants no bubbling and no queue jump. Fix: add one sentence — appetite bounds SCOPE only and is **order-neutral**; only priority [T-11] moves lane position; a small appetite is **not** a quick win (a wish can carry a half-day appetite AND normal priority). | should-clarify · missing-rule (invariant) | **FOLDED**: appetite bends scope only, never order — a half-day appetite is not a quick-win mark; only priority moves the lane (T-11 cited) |
| F4 | **INV-20's own wording makes a missing non-goal both a valid meaning and a defect.** INV-20 (L155): "**absent non-goals mean nothing was excluded on purpose, AND the prover reads silence as a hole again.**" These conjoin two incompatible readings of absence: (a) absence carries a MEANING ("nothing excluded") — a legitimate state; (b) absence is a DEFECT the prover flags. If (a), the prover must NOT flag it; if (b), every feature must WRITE the sentence. INV-18 (L120) resolved the identical shape unambiguously — "silence is not an option," and a surface with nothing to say writes an explicit "no visible surface — facets N/A," never a silent skip. Fix by that precedent: every feature WRITES a non-goals sentence; "nothing deliberately left out this time" is itself a valid explicit sentence; only true ABSENCE (no sentence at all) is the hole the prover flags. Drop the "absent non-goals mean nothing was excluded" half — it grants a silent skip the next clause revokes. | should-clarify · internal-conflict (consistency) | **FOLDED**: the non-goals sentence is ALWAYS written; "nothing deliberately left out this time" is valid; only a missing sentence is a hole (INV-18 mirror) |
| F5 | **Non-goals have no surfacing path — a senior can silently narrow scope.** INV-21 explicitly routes its questions to the batched report ("the quantification questions … ride the facet sweep's batched report" — L159); INV-20 routes non-goals **nowhere** for human visibility — the non-goal is written for "a later reader — and the prover" (L154), never surfaced to YOU at decide-time. But a non-goal ("version comparison — not this time") is a **scope decision**, exactly the class INV-5 (L176) forbids to bury: "every choice not in your wish is either asked, or recorded in the spec AND surfaced in the same report." As written the senior can author an over-narrow non-goal (silently dropping something you'd have wanted) and it only surfaces when you later read the spec. Fix: the non-goals sentence **rides the same batched report** as the facet defaults and INV-21's questions, so an over-narrow scope becomes a new wish — the facet-veto pattern (INV-18) applied to non-goals. | should-clarify · missing-outcome-check (postcondition) | **FOLDED**: a scope-narrowing non-goal rides the same batched report as taken defaults (INV-4/INV-18 channel), never silent (INV-5 cited) |
| F6 | **Reusing INV-18's `[default]` tag drags in a matrix-row implication INV-21 then contradicts.** INV-18 (L124) defines `[default]` as carrying a matrix consequence: a defaulted facet is tagged "so … the matrix derives the facet's **test row** either way [E-15]." INV-21 (L158) reuses the literal tag ("decided or `[default]`-tagged **like any facet**") for the success measure — but INV-21 then says the measure gets NO testable row: the reading machinery is [target] and "**a success measure is a written promise the human checks by eye**" (L160). So the same tag implies "matrix derives a row" on a facet and "no row, eyeball it" on a success measure — E-15's coverage walk ("every spec anchor appears in ≥1 row") cannot be run deterministically against a `[default]` success measure. Fix: state that a success-measure `[default]` marks **provenance only** (human-decided vs recommended-taken) and derives **no matrix row until the reading machinery [target] lands** — distinct from a facet's `[default]`, whose row derives now. | should-clarify · boundary-issue (composition) | **FOLDED**: the reused `[default]` tag marks provenance only — no matrix row derives from a success measure while the reading machinery stays [target] |
| F7 | **"Every feature" is silent on retroactivity — do already-adopted/re-engineered features owe a non-goal + success measure?** INV-20/INV-21 both say "**every feature**" (L153, L156) with no scoping. Adoption re-engineers existing features into SPEC.md sections (A-3, L248) and promotes de-facto surfaces "at the spec step as a feature" (A-10, L253); INV-18 explicitly handled this seam ("On an adopted or promoted surface … a default is read from the shipped truth … never invented greenfield" — L129). INV-20/INV-21 say nothing, so read literally they demand a retroactive non-goal + measure on every already-adopted feature at adoption time — a burden A-3 never mentions and INV-15's precedent forbids ("the invariant binds from the landing that creates it, **never retroactively**" — L410). Fix: state INV-20/INV-21 bind from the feature-delta landing under them; an adopted feature owes them at the **first landing that touches it** (mirroring A-3's reconcile-on-first-touch), not retroactively across the adopted set; a promoted surface owes them as it enters the spec step. | should-clarify · missing-scenario (state-space) | **FOLDED**: both sentences bind forward; an adopted feature owes its pair at the first landing that touches it (A-3), never retroactively en masse |
| F8 | **Prototype carve-out present for facets and fences, absent for non-goals and success measure — the exact class the fence pass just folded.** T-13 got an explicit sketch exemption ("A fenced prototype is NOT swept — a sketch has no facets to promise" — L118), and the prior pass (`-fences` F7) deliberately ADDED the parallel to T-14 ("a prototype fences nothing because it promises nothing" — L150) as a standing convention. INV-20/INV-21 repeat the omission — covered by construction (a prototype has no spec-delta: "no lane, no spec" — L206), so nothing broken ships, but the pack's own just-established sibling convention says make it explicit or the reader re-runs the same wondering. Fix (sibling-sweep, base rule 14): add one half-sentence — "a prototype states no non-goals and no success measure — it promises nothing [E-17]." | worth-considering · missing-scenario (state-space) | **FOLDED**: prototype carve-out now explicit — a prototype writes neither sentence, it promises nothing (E-17), matching T-13/T-14 |
| F9 | **Appetite "trims scope" is not bounded against INV-18 facet completeness — could read as "drop a facet to fit half a day."** T-15: "**Scope bends to fit the appetite**" (L63); INV-18: every visible facet MUST end as a sentence, "silence is not an option" (L120). A reader can take "scope bends" to mean skipping the a11y or phone facet on a kept surface to hit the budget — which INV-18 forbids. T-15's own "plainest default … considered option" (L66) is the LEGITIMATE appetite lever (facet RICHNESS), never facet PRESENCE. Also unstated: what default richness applies when NO appetite is named (L65 says defaults size to a *named* appetite). Fix: state appetite trims **scope** (which surfaces/behaviours are in), never facet **presence** on a kept surface — a shipped surface owes its full facet sweep at whatever richness the appetite affords; no-appetite ⇒ the existing INV-18 recommended default. | worth-considering · over-general (abstraction) | **FOLDED**: a trim may cut which surfaces are in and how considered the defaults are — never whether a kept surface's facets get their sentences; no-appetite default stated |

Nine findings, outcomes PENDING for the senior. F1 (must-fix) folds before the M-6 push or the delta does
not ship; F2/F3 pin appetite's place and order-neutrality; F4/F5 fix INV-20's self-conflict and its missing
surfacing path; F6 scopes the reused `[default]` tag; F7 pins retroactivity via the INV-15/A-3 precedent;
F8/F9 are the prototype sibling-sweep and the scope-vs-facet bound. The FULL push-gate pass owed for the
MINOR bump (process note above) is where the whole-spec re-prove lands.

All nine findings folded same sitting by the senior (Fable) -> SPEC v0.13.0 final wording; the MINOR-under-CROSS-LINK FULL debt discharges at the 1.0 milestone audit. Nothing left for the queue from this pass.

19	the author-side verdict and the folds. The orchestrator runs the required independent fresh-eyes
20	adversarial pass (INV-46 — this edits the method itself) and the deep whole-spec pass before push.

23	
24	1. **INV-151 — a request enters at the highest document its change reaches, and the door set is CLOSED.**
25	   The derivation chain (spec → architecture → matrix → code → docs, the settings ladder beside it for a
26	   pure value) is walked top-down: the first document whose sentences must change is the entry layer, and
27	   the request flows down from there through every step its door grants. The set of entry points is
28	   enumerated and closed — product behaviour, a technically-phrased request, a defect, docs-only, a tiny
29	   reversible edit, a settings value, an inbox wish, a method/skill change, a sketch, research, and a
30	   feedback hand-back — each with its home and its mandatory back-check. The spec-motion back-check for a
31	   technically-phrased request fires AT INTAKE (the tripwires decide before entry and outrank the request's
32	   own label, INV-16) and re-fires mid-work, so a lift to the spec happens before architecture work is
33	   built on an unlifted premise. A request that matches no kind becomes one plain question (INV-4), never a
34	   guessed route. The method change is NOT a separate meta-layer set: the pack's product is the method, so
35	   a method change enters by the same criterion with work-kind skill scaling each step's form (section 8).
36	
37	2. **INV-152 — a deferral must justify itself, or the item is the seat's to do.** A held work item carrying
38	   a needs-the-human's-word marker (a queue row, a NEXT_STEPS line, an open setup-script decision) is
39	   re-tested by derivability every time it is touched. An answer pinning to an existing artifact makes the
40	   item the seat's (do it, cite the artifact, drop the marker); an answer needing a fact no artifact holds
41	   (a taste, a policy, an act irreversible outside git) makes it the human's. Writing such a marker requires
42	   naming that human-only fact; a marker that cannot name it defaults to the seat's, and a marker that
43	   cannot say why the item is the human's is itself the finding — the same shape as a request matching no
44	   kind. Its normative home is base rulebook rule 29; the spec clause states it.
45	
46	3. **INV-153 — the unification, stated once.** The request classifier (INV-151), the property net (INV-150),
47	   and the deferral test (INV-152) are one principle: every incoming thing routes to the home whose declared
48	   sentence governs it, and a thing that pins to no home is itself the finding. They stay three separate
49	   controls under the one principle because they run at different moments under different verifiers — the
50	   classifier by the applied-or-stood-down-by-name landing contract (INV-22), the property net by the
51	   declared-laws station (INV-101), the deferral test by the derive-before-defer posture (INV-143). No new

62	| INV-152 ↔ INV-143 | the deferral test is the seat's decide-what-it-can-decide posture applied to a work item | consistent — INV-143 already holds the posture on every session including a wipe-resumed one; INV-152 sharpens it to the marker's write and re-test moment, kin not duplicate (INV-143 is the general posture, INV-152 the marker discipline) |

70	door step. This is the spec-states-the-contract / skill-states-the-machinery split the pack uses everywhere
71	(INV-22, E-12): the table's per-kind home is build-pipeline, the spec names the closed-set law. Not a
72	one-home violation — the spec does not re-table the machinery, it points at the door step. `acknowledged ·
73	composition`
74	
75	**F2 — no live inbox item exercises the deferral clause's seat-default path (acknowledged).**
76	INV-152 is testable in prose and its shape is exercised by the classifier's fallback, but the pack has no
77	live held work item today whose marker fails to name a human-only fact. The clause is exercised the day a

   item the seat's (do it, cite the artifact, drop the marker); an answer needing a fact no artifact holds
   (a taste, a policy, an act irreversible outside git) makes it the human's. Writing such a marker requires
   naming that human-only fact; a marker that cannot name it defaults to the seat's, and a marker that
   cannot say why the item is the human's is itself the finding — the same shape as a request matching no
   kind. Its normative home is base rulebook rule 29; the spec clause states it.

3. **INV-153 — the unification, stated once.** The request classifier (INV-151), the property net (INV-150),
   and the deferral test (INV-152) are one principle: every incoming thing routes to the home whose declared
   sentence governs it, and a thing that pins to no home is itself the finding. They stay three separate
   controls under the one principle because they run at different moments under different verifiers — the
   classifier by the applied-or-stood-down-by-name landing contract (INV-22), the property net by the
   declared-laws station (INV-101), the deferral test by the derive-before-defer posture (INV-143). No new
   machinery beyond writing the door set as closed and the fallback question.

## Seams checked

| seam | claim | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| INV-151 ↔ INV-16 | the spec-motion back-check fires at intake and outranks the label | consistent — INV-16's tripwires already decide before entry and outrank a casual label; INV-151 names the intake moment as the back-check's home, the audit's refinement (2) folded (moment moved to the door, not a post-entry back-check) |
| INV-151 ↔ INV-128 | the entry-layer read and the three-source footprint read are one intake, not two | consistent — the footprint reads reach (which layers), the classifier reads entry (highest layer that changes); both fire at the same intake moment, the footprint composing with the door as INV-128 already states |
| INV-151 closed set ↔ the pack's homes | every enumerated kind has a real home in the pack | consistent — spec/architecture/matrix/skip/settings-ladder/inbox-wish/sketch/research/feedback each cite an existing clause or skill (E-13, INV-17, E-17, T-20); no kind invented |
| INV-151 meta-layer collapse ↔ section 8 | a method change needs no separate set | consistent — the design-reviewer's own birth (INV-141/142 → architecture node → skill) is the worked proof the audit cites; the tripwire re-doors a method change that alters what a session does |
| INV-152 ↔ INV-143 | the deferral test is the seat's decide-what-it-can-decide posture applied to a work item | consistent — INV-143 already holds the posture on every session including a wipe-resumed one; INV-152 sharpens it to the marker's write and re-test moment, kin not duplicate (INV-143 is the general posture, INV-152 the marker discipline) |
| INV-152 ↔ INV-151 | a marker that cannot name its human-only fact is the same shape as a request matching no kind | consistent — both are the homeless-item finding; INV-151 and INV-152 cross-reference, INV-153 states the shared shape once |

**F1 — the closed set lives in two homes (the spec clause and the build-pipeline table), by design (acknowledged).**
INV-151's enumeration is stated compactly in the spec clause and in full table form at build-pipeline's
door step. This is the spec-states-the-contract / skill-states-the-machinery split the pack uses everywhere
(INV-22, E-12): the table's per-kind home is build-pipeline, the spec names the closed-set law. Not a
one-home violation — the spec does not re-table the machinery, it points at the door step. `acknowledged ·
composition`

**F2 — no live inbox item exercises the deferral clause's seat-default path (acknowledged).**
INV-152 is testable in prose and its shape is exercised by the classifier's fallback, but the pack has no
live held work item today whose marker fails to name a human-only fact. The clause is exercised the day a

  section 8 into "the same criterion, work-kind skill", with the design-reviewer's own landing named as the
  worked proof — the pack's product IS the method, so no meta-layer set exists.

## Verdict

The delta holds together as written. The closed set names every request kind a home in the existing pack,
the fallback question closes the between-layers gap the audit asked for, the deferral clause applies the
no-homeless-item control to a work item, and the unification states the one principle once without merging
the two controls or adding machinery. No blocking defect remains in the author-side pass. The suite is
green at 736 (12 new assertions), `guardrails/check-shipped-language.sh` clean. The version stays held; the

# live-spec — overnight decisions page (2026-07-06 night, session 22)

**NEEDS YOUR WORD — in the morning, nothing burns: 1 decision below.** Night's total: 25 rows landed
and pushed · 23 new laws (all five of his night corrections + all eight promoter-audit lessons) ·
suite 134 → 162 green · the public repo now runs its own gates in CI. Everything else tonight is
just updates (chat carries them); no action needed there. The interactive version of this page (pick
an option, add your word, save the JSON) is the .html twin opened in your browser — this .md is the
repo record.

Kill-list of this artifact (his review rounds, INV-42):
- Round 1 (~23:38): the first before/after sample — KILLED, both halves «непонятно ни до ни после»;
  the bar he set: tone of voice of the most qualified persona who owns that stage (a strong product
  manager for product sections, a strong engineering lead for process sections). Never resurface the
  round-1 phrasing.
- Round 1b (~23:40, on his quotes): **pack coinages as reader-facing words — KILLED** («the wish being
  built»: a human text says task, feature, work in progress; internal nicknames stay internal) and
  **filler openers — KILLED** («Here is exactly what happens» is noise; a rule starts with the rule).
  Both applied to round 2 below.
- Round 2 (2026-07-07 ~07:59, morning verdict): **the rule-book genre itself — KILLED** («это все
  равно плохо»). Numbered laws in an owner's voice still read as regulation, not product. The bar he
  set: write in the language of USE CASES and FEATURE DESCRIPTIONS — the reader follows a person doing
  something and what the product does for them; study BMAD-METHOD and Kiro spec formats (user stories,
  acceptance criteria) for the shape. Round 3 = use-case-genre sample.

---

## Decision 1 — the spec-readability rewrite (row 148, mockup-first entry)

Your word (~23:24): specs should read as if a qualified human wrote them. Below is round 2 of the
sample — two real SPEC sections rewritten in the voice you named. If it fits, the whole document gets
this treatment section by section (rule content and anchors held identical, full prover re-check
after). If not — say what to change; your correction becomes the bar.

### Sample A — a product rule, written by a strong product manager

**NOW IN THE SPEC (v0.15.42):**

> **An approved look lives in its artifact — the clause that encodes it points there, and the build looks
> at it.** Text cannot carry a feel: a spec clause born of an approved visual prototype was once rebuilt
> from its own prose and shipped a cheap look-alike — 75 tests green, because tests derived from a misread
> spec prove the misreading (tlvphoto's door and gallery, 2026-07-05). So when the human approves a sketch
> as the look, the prototype becomes the **norm** for look and feel, and one law with four arms guards it.
> The clause CITES its artifact — a `norm: <path>` pointer at the clause's line end beside its anchors,
> the prose carrying the laws while the artifact keeps the look (spec-author owns the pointer's format). …

**PROPOSED (round 2):**

> **Approved prototypes are binding design references**
>
> When you approve a prototype ("this is the door"), that prototype — not the text describing it —
> becomes the reference for how the feature must look and feel.
>
> 1. **The spec links to the reference.** Any requirement born from an approved prototype ends with a
>    pointer to the file: `norm: docs/norms/door.html`.
> 2. **Approval freezes a copy.** The approved file is copied into `docs/norms/` with a short note:
>    what it is, when it was approved, which sketch it came from. Requirements point only at this
>    frozen copy — never at a working sketch, which may still change or be deleted.
> 3. **Builders open the reference before building.** Whoever implements such a requirement opens the
>    prototype first and records one line: how the plan differs from it. Work that skipped this is
>    rejected at review, and the final check judges look and feel against the same reference.
> 4. **"Show me a mockup first" is a recorded requirement.** It is written into the task itself, and
>    only you can cancel it — by saying so explicitly. A general "go ahead and build" does not cancel
>    it.
>
> Why this exists: a gallery was once rebuilt from its text description alone, without opening the
> approved prototype. All 75 tests passed — they had been derived from the same misread text. What
> shipped looked nothing like what was approved. (tlvphoto, 2026-07-05) [INV-43]

### Sample B — a process rule, written by a strong engineering lead

**NOW IN THE SPEC:**

> A bug may interrupt the wish in-work. The interrupted wish moves to **parked**: a checkpoint is written
> (failing test names if red, hypothesis, touched files — nothing red is ever committed), the bug takes the
> lane, and the parked wish resumes as the immediate next landing — ahead of ANY queued wish, a quick win
> included: a bubble [T-11] jumps only fresh queued wishes, never a resume. …

**PROPOSED (round 2):**

> **When a bug interrupts: the fixed sequence**

588:## Requirement 16: Every wish is placed on the feature map by one of three verdicts
589-
590-**Context:** Every wish is placed on the product's feature map, and the placement is stated by default. The feature map is the spec's scenario sections and the architecture's nodes together, so no separate map document exists. Each placement is one of three verdicts: it changes an existing feature, it is a new feature, or it is a restructure.
591-
592-**User Story:** As a person tracking where a wish lands in the product, I want its placement stated and recorded as one of three verdicts, so that the map stays the spec plus the architecture and a restructure opens its own row rather than re-dividing on the spot.
593-
--
3641:## Requirement 160: A bug preempts the lane, and rolling features park  [feature: F-bug]
3642-
3643-**Context:** Mid-feature, the human reports a bug in the shipped product — the card is broken on the phone. The feature in work is set aside at a checkpoint, the bug takes the lane, and once no bug waits the feature returns as the next thing to finish. When nothing is in work, the bug takes the lane directly.
3644-
3645-**User Story:** As the product owner, I want a reported bug fixed before anything else while the mid-build feature comes back on its own afterward, so that an urgent defect is handled at once and no in-flight work is lost.
3646-
--
3668:## Requirement 161: A confirmed bug drives a class hunt before it closes  [feature: F-bug]
3669-
3670-**Context:** A confirmed bug is one sample of its class. Before the fix is called done, the method drives four moves rather than one — name the class and hunt its siblings, check the architecture, check the spec, and escalate a boundary call to the human — so a point fix that leaves the rest of the class standing is a status, never a landing.
3671-
3672-**User Story:** As the product owner, I want a confirmed bug treated as one instance of a class and its siblings hunted before the fix closes, so that the same kind of defect is cleared everywhere it lives, hunted past the one place it happened to show.
3673-
--
3694:## Requirement 162: The problem ledger holds the workshop's own noise  [feature: F-problem-ledger]
3695-
3696-**Context:** Some noise comes from the workshop itself: a test harness or tool flakes at random, a dependency goes missing, a shell command fails for a reason outside the product, a tool times out. A session retries and moves on, and then the same noise eats the same minutes session after session. A flaky test the project itself owns is a different thing, a defect fixed at its root and never workshop noise.
3697-
3698-**User Story:** As a person losing minutes to recurring operational noise, I want each workshop problem recorded in one ledger with a status, so that noise seen twice gets a tracked owner instead of being rediscovered and retried each session.
3699-
--
3714:## Requirement 163: The ledger walk and its two-strikes ladder  [feature: F-problem-ledger]
3715-
3716-**Context:** The moment noise fires mid-work, the session greps the ledger for the signature, and what the grep returns decides the next move. The walk climbs a fixed ladder from a first sighting to a method defect.
3717-
3718-**User Story:** As a person meeting operational noise mid-work, I want the ledger walk to record a first sighting, buy an owner on the second, and escalate a third unowned recurrence to the pack, so that a problem seen twice is never silently retried and a method defect reaches the pack's own queue.
3719-
--
3741:## Requirement 164: A resolved entry collects dates and archives at the milestone  [feature: F-problem-ledger]
3742-
3743-**Context:** Once an entry has its owner, it only collects dates. A recurrence appends a date and changes nothing else, and a landing that closes the owning row flips the entry closed in the same session rather than waiting for an audit.
3744-
3745-**User Story:** As a person tracking an owned problem, I want a recurrence to only append its date and a landing to close the entry at once, so that the ledger stays current without a recurrence reopening a settled verdict or an audit lagging the truth.
3746-
--
3764:## Requirement 165: A known owned problem stays parked while unrelated work rolls  [feature: F-problem-ledger]
3765-
3766-**Context:** A known, owned problem never blocks unrelated work; it stays parked while every unrelated lane keeps rolling. It is either a recurring defect with a named mechanical owner or a check held red for an understood, recorded reason, held in place by its ledger line, its owning row, or an expected-red note.
3767-
3768-**User Story:** As a person with one known problem parked, I want every unrelated lane to keep rolling and the problem's instances serviced in batch, so that one thing not quite working never blocks the rest and never interrupts the work with a per-instance ceremony.
3769-
--
3788:## Requirement 166: The ledger's seams and the scope of this landing  [feature: F-problem-ledger]
3789-
3790-**Context:** The ledger's seams state who writes it, how two sessions share it, when two entries are one problem, and where the workshop's law ends and the product's begins. The landing opens the pack's own ledger and leaves the mechanical guard for later.
3791-
3792-**User Story:** As a person maintaining the ledger across sessions and workers, I want its write-ownership, concurrency, and merge rules stated and this landing's scope named, so that a worker's noise reaches the ledger safely, two sessions never clobber it, and one problem under two wordings becomes one entry.
3793-
--
3821:## Requirement 167: Search for an existing skill before reinventing a fix  [feature: F-problem-ledger]
3822-
3823-**Context:** Before reinventing a fix, the pack searches for an existing skill. Two moments trigger the search: a project's setup, and a struggle that keeps returning. A found skill is adopted or rejected by name, and borrowing keeps to one practice.
3824-
3825-**User Story:** As a person about to reinvent a fix, I want the pack to search for an existing skill at setup and at every struggle, so that a returning failure class is met by something that already owns it, sparing a fresh build from scratch.
3826-
--
3839:## Requirement 168: The version-control gate runs before the first delivery
3840-
3841-**Context:** Every host reaches its first delivery through the same gate, and both a fresh start and an attach run it in the same order. A gate cannot protect files older than itself, so the gate runs before anything is created or moved. The gate settles two things: that git exists, and that a remote either exists or is declined on the record.
3842-
3843-**User Story:** As a person starting or attaching a host, I want the version-control gate settled before the first delivery, so that no work is committed somewhere it cannot be recovered or tracked.
3844-
--
3863:## Requirement 169: Bootstrapping a fresh host  [feature: F-bootstrap]
3864-
3865-**Context:** A fresh host starts from the templates the pack ships. The system copies the document set and the suite scaffold, then the first request enters the queue and runs through the ordinary pipeline. The scaffold's green is the starting floor the first delivery builds on.
3866-
3867-**User Story:** As a person starting a fresh host, I want the templates and a runnable scaffold in place, so that the first request runs through the ordinary pipeline against a known starting floor. [B-1]
3868-

## Итоговый отчёт

**Методологическая находка (важна сама по себе):** из 20 указанных «крупнейших» файлов транскриптов в `~/.claude/projects/-Users-sashaabramovich-live-spec/`, **18 оказались автоматическими «register judge» прогонами** (проверка стиля текста), а не рабочими сессиями с хозяином — в них роль `user` это судейский rubric-промпт, не человек. Реальных рабочих сессий с несколькими репликами хозяина всего **2**: `04cf12be…jsonl` и `277bd5b2…jsonl` (обе 2026‑08‑13, read-only архитектурные сессии про «LiveSpec vNext»). Я проверил это независимо (скриптом по всем 1333 файлам проекта) и получил тот же результат, что и параллельный агент — расхождений нет. Ни в этих двух сессиях, ни в JOURNAL.md/DECISIONS.md/ROADMAP.md **не найдено дословных терминов** «сквозной/локальный», «раздел/подфункционал» как классификационной лексики хозяина — эти конкретные слова в корпусе не встречаются.

### Прескрипции хозяина — сильнейшие подтверждённые дословные цитаты

- **Учредительная формулировка цепочки документов** (самая близкая находка к описанной «intake chain»), `docs/decisions/2026-07-05-decisions.json`, note к решению `package-name`, 2026-07-05 08:49:45 UTC:
  > «в лайвспек потерялся тест спек. про то как строится матрица. то есть у нас есть продакт спека типа там юскейсы человеческим языком и глобально абстракт или чето такое придумай сам, потом прувер, потом архитектура, потом возможно прувер на архитектуру (или как сам решишь, ага?) потом спек тестов матрица покрытие валидация на всех уровнях, понял... ну и далее.»
  (En gloss: "live-spec lost its test spec — how the matrix gets built. ### Что НЕ найдено, но существует как формализованный (ассистентский) след цепочки

Точной устной формулировки «сквозной/локальный; новый/правка; раздел/подфункционал» в доступном корпусе нет. Но её кодифицированный, ассистентом написанный эквивалент живёт в PRODUCT_SPEC.md:
- **Requirement 16** (L588): «Every wish is placed on the feature map by one of three verdicts: it changes an existing feature, it is a new feature, or it is a restructure» — формальный аналог «новый / правка».
- **Requirement 40** (L1057): классификация в «door» ∈ {feature, bug, refactor, docs-only, skip}.
- **Requirement 43** (L1122): «footprint» ∈ {presentation-only, single-module, cross-cutting}, читается разом из spec+architecture+code на одном intake-моменте — формальный аналог «локальный/сквозной».
- **Requirement 44** (L1155): footprint обязателен в строке очереди, суточный чек красит строку без него.
- **Requirement 45** (L1174): запрос входит в самый верхний документ цепочки spec→architecture→test-matrix→code→docs.
- Также `docs/pipeline.md` (станции 1–11, `spec → prove → architecture → prove architecture → matrix → test → code → verify → commit → show`) — целиком написан ассистентом, но описывает именно ту цепочку, которую хозяин впервые продиктовал 2026-07-05.
